turns.content: A spring has natural length 10 cm and requires a 40 N holding force at length 15 cm. What is its extension from the natural length, expressed in metres?
Take extension as positive in the stretching direction. What ordered pair (extension, holding force) describes the calibration measurement in SI units?
Assuming Hooke's law, use that calibration pair to determine the spring constant and state its units.
As the spring changes from 15 cm to 18 cm, what are the corresponding lower and upper temperature rises from its natural length, expressed in metres?
Set up and evaluate the work integral for this stretch using the Hooke-law force and the extension bounds found above.
Verify the result independently by taking the change in elastic potential energy between the two extensions.
What sign should the work done by the applied stretching force have over this outward displacement, and why?
Give the work required to stretch the spring from 15 cm to 18 cm, with units and the appropriate sign.
